overview: Spicy's LongJump is a one-shot horizontal impulse module that labels itself 'Hypixel'. Enabling it forges a C13PacketPlayerAbilities claiming flying, creative mode and a randomized fly speed between 0.1 and 9.0, pushed through sendPacketNoEvent so the module's own event bus never sees it — on servers that trust the abilities packet this arms the client with flight. The movement half runs on EventMotion post: the jump key is forced off, and on the first post-move tick whose bounding-box probe reports ground contact, the module re-aims the player's horizontal motion at the current speed plus a flat 1.25 boost (MovementUtils.strafe(speed + 1.25f)), fires jump(), and latches a jumped flag so the next grounded post-event toggles the module off. The result is a single jump carrying roughly 1.4 blocks per tick of horizontal velocity — an order of magnitude above the sprint-jump envelope — that ends the moment the player lands.

sections.p: onEnable builds a PlayerCapabilities with isFlying, allowFlying and isCreativeMode all true and a flySpeed drawn uniformly from 0.1 to 9.0, serializes it into a C13PacketPlayerAbilities and sends it through the network manager's sendPacketNoEvent. The randomized fly speed is deliberate noise; the claims themselves are the payload. The additionalInformation field is stamped 'Hypixel' on every pre-update, the module's own statement of where it is meant to run: servers that filter the abilities packet and leave only the movement burst to be judged.

onEvent runs on EventMotion post, which Spicy's onUpdateWalkingPlayer dispatches at the end of the tick, after the tick's C03 has already been sent. keyBindJump.pressed is forced false so the vanilla jump input cannot stack a second impulse. When the ground probe — MovementUtils.isOnGround(0.000001), an actual bounding-box intersection 0.000001 below the feet rather than the onGround flag — succeeds, the module reads the current horizontal speed from motionX/motionZ, calls strafe(speed + 1.25f) to rewrite motion along the movement yaw, calls jump() (motionY = 0.42), sets jumped and cancels the event. The next tick's C03 therefore reports a horizontal displacement of roughly 1.4 blocks with a jump vertical. The event cancel is a no-op in this fork — onUpdateWalkingPlayer sends the C03 unconditionally — so the burst is a pure one-tick velocity artifact, and the landing check (jumped && onGround) toggles the module off so the boost is never sustained.

files.label: LongJump.java (module)
files.explanation:
The module has three distinct regions. The enable handler forges the abilities packet with the randomized fly speed. The EventUpdate pre branch writes the 'Hypixel' hint. The EventMotion post branch is the exploit: it force-releases the jump key, waits for the 0.000001 ground probe, then strafes to speed + 1.25, jumps and latches jumped; the same branch toggles the module off on the first grounded tick after the latch, and the static Timer field is declared but never used.

The latch logic is the whole lifecycle: enable once, burst once, disable on landing. Because the strafe and jump happen after the tick's C03 is already on the wire, the server sees the boosted velocity only in the following C03 — one anomalous move, then ordinary motion until the module turns itself off.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (impulse helpers)
files.explanation:
Two helpers the module leans on. isOnGround(height) intersects the entity bounding box offset downward by height against the world's collision boxes (getCollidingBoundingBoxes) — a world probe, not the packet's onGround flag — which is why the module can trust it for the ground latch. strafe(speed) recomputes motionX and motionZ from getDirection(), which folds moveForward and moveStrafing into the player's yaw with the standard 45-degree diagonal rules, and bails out if there is no movement input at all.

The module adds the 1.25 itself: strafe(getSpeed() + 1.25f) preserves whatever horizontal velocity already exists and adds a flat 1.25 m/tick on top, which is what turns a normal jump into the ~1.4 m/tick burst the anticheats see.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed movement from the world. The horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation, whose sprint prediction caps a sprinting move near 0.286 blocks per tick, and the vertical from vDistRel's momentum-seeded envelopes, which accept a zero-y grounded move, a jump, a step-up and a riptide launch. The violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0)) * 100, with handleViolation set-backs to the stored location.

The module's burst C03 carries a horizontal displacement of about 1.4 blocks in one tick — roughly five times the sprint-predicted allowance — so hDistanceAboveLimit lands near 1.1 and the result exceeds 100 on the first burst move: an immediate violation and set-back. The jump's vertical (0.42) would fit the jump envelope on its own; the horizontal is what detonates the check. The forged C13 is irrelevant to the envelope: NCP models the player from the server's own capability state, and SurvivalFly grants no fly envelope to a player whose server-side abilities do not allow flying.

countering.label: Speed (off-ground stage model)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed compares per-move horizontal distance against expected values derived from a 0.2873 base move speed (scaled by speed potions) plus stage constants chosen by vertical speed: 0.049 for a flat glide, 0.08 for a low ascent and 0.3261 for a jump-arc tick. The off-ground branch also folds in any recent knockback velocity tracked through VelocityData, then flags 'Moving too fast, offground_expected (BunnyHop)' when thisMove exceeds the expectation.

For the burst move, thisMove ≈ 1.4 against an expectation around 0.61 (base plus jump stage) with no velocity credit — the violation fires on the single anomalous C03, and data.setSetback rolls the player back to the previous location. The check is per-move, so the one-tick nature of the module's burst does not save it: the anomalous move is the move that is checked.

countering.label: Speed (momentum discrepancy model)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Speed predicts the next move from the previous one: expected = friction * lastSpeed * multipliers + maxForce + adders, with a 0.2 adder for a sprinting jump, and accumulates the discrepancy between expected and actual speed across moves. A positive discrepancy over the 0.1 threshold (DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD) at a position update triggers punishAndTryRubberband with the VL scaled by VL_FAIL_DISCREPANCY_FACTOR.

On the burst move, lastSpeed is walking speed (~0.1-0.2) and maxForce is the vanilla input force (~0.1), so expected lands near 0.2 while the actual move is ~1.4 — a discrepancy around 1.2, over twelve times the threshold — so the rubberband fires on the first position update after the impulse. The module's 1.25 boost is precisely the kind of raw velocity addition the momentum model exists to measure, and because the boost is a single move, the cumulative discrepancy is maximal on that one move.
